turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning, Mr Naidoo. Before the doctor calls you I've done the observations. Blood pressure is one thirty-eight over eighty-six, pulse seventy-four, and the temperature is thirty-six point eight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Morning, I'm Doctor Pillay. Sit if that foot allows it. What's going on?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Toe.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Shame, man. It's his big toe, the right one, terribly sore. He was awake half the night.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): When did it start?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Last night.
[SEG0008] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sudden, about eleven, after we got back from—
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the pain in that toe, out of ten?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Nine.
[SEG0012] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, nine. That right toe came on sudden about eleven last night, and the sheet was agony on it. We left the dog at home, he'd only climb on the foot.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Is it swollen?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0015] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Red and hot, this side, over the joint. He won't let me near it.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or are you feeling generally unwell?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you knock it at all? Stub it, or—
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0020] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hang on. You kicked the chair in the passage yesterday, you were—
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag. Ja. Chair.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Was the toe already sore before the kick, or only afterwards?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): After. No - last night.
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The kick was in the afternoon. He ate supper fine, then it blew up.

[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me check I have this straight. The right big toe has been at a nine out of ten since last night and it's swollen, and you kicked a chair yesterday afternoon but supper was still fine. Fair?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0027] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Same thing about a year back, same toe. The chemist gave him something, I can't remember the name, and it settled in a few days.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): And did anyone call it gout that time?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you on any tablets at the moment?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Water tablet.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you know the name, or the strength?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Um.
[SEG0034] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's hydrochlorothiazide, twenty-five milligrams, one every morning, for his blood pressure. He's been on it, what, two years?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything besides that? Did you take something for pain this morning?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about drink?
[SEG0039] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Beers at the weekend. Friday and Saturday, maybe four or five each night, nothing in the week. Ag, the parking nearly made us late, we drove—
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): So that's beers Friday and Saturday, about four or five, and nothing in the week. I'll look at the foot.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): The right big toe joint is hot, swollen and very tender to touch. Skin's intact, there's no break. The other joints on the foot look normal.
[SEG0043] person_1 (NURSE): Should I book the bloods, doctor?

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, please. I'd like a serum uric acid, a full blood count and a CRP today. I think this is most likely an acute gout flare, though with that knock I can't fully exclude a bit of trauma as well.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll start colchicine, nought point five milligrams by mouth twice a day for three days, and take it with food.

[SEG0046] person_3 (DOCTOR): If your tummy can't tolerate the colchicine, stop it and switch to naproxen five hundred milligrams twice a day with food, but not both together. If it's not easing in three days, come back and see me, or sooner if you get a fever or the redness spreads up the foot.
